site.name: PGX_AI Adventures
site.tagline: Weekly AI prototypes and experiments on a desk-sized Grace Blackwell workstation.
site.description: A public lab notebook: one AI prototype or experiment every week on a Lenovo ThinkStation PGX (NVIDIA GB10 Grace Blackwell, 128 GB unified memory), with reproducible code, raw results and provenance for every run.

programme.label: Week
programme.cadence: One experiment folder lands in the repository every week.
programme.roadmapIntro: The programme runs 52 weeks: 26 general AI-engineering weeks alternating with 26 signature research weeks.

roadmap.title: Platform baseline
roadmap.blurb: Reproducible PyTorch throughput and correctness on the GB10, pinned to a container digest.

roadmap.title: GPU observability and energy per result
roadmap.blurb: Paired monitoring-on/off runs to measure what observing the GPU costs, plus sensor-domain energy per matrix multiply.

roadmap.title: Arm64 / SM121 framework compatibility atlas
roadmap.blurb: Which frameworks, wheels and kernels actually run natively on the GB10's compute-capability-12.1 GPU.

roadmap.title: Local LLM serving
roadmap.blurb: Open-weight models from the 128 GB unified memory: quantisation, context length and tokens per second.

roadmap.title: NanoChat
roadmap.blurb: Training a small chat model end to end on a single desk-side machine.

roadmap.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
roadmap.blurb: Local embeddings, vector search and grounded answers over private documents.

roadmap.title: Agents
roadmap.blurb: Tool-using agents running fully on-device, with an eye on cost, latency and safety.

roadmap.title: Time-series models and digital twins
roadmap.blurb: Forecasting and anomaly detection on sensor data with modern sequence models.

roadmap.title: AI security
roadmap.blurb: Confidential RAG, fully homomorphic encryption, cyber-defence and adversarial robustness — the signature research weeks.

author.name: Alvin
author.bio: I enjoy AI and cybersecurity research. PGX_AI_Adventures is my public, weekly lab notebook, where every experiment runs on my personal ThinkStation PGX machine, and everything (code, container digest, etc.) needed to reproduce it is published alongside the write-up.

machine.name: Lenovo ThinkStation PGX
machine.intro: The whole programme runs on one small workstation — a 150 mm square box that puts a Blackwell GPU, a 20-core Arm CPU and 128 GB of memory on a single coherent memory pool. That unified memory is the reason a desk-side machine can hold models that would not fit on a typical discrete GPU.

specs.label: Architecture
specs.value: NVIDIA Blackwell, 48 streaming multiprocessors (6,144 CUDA cores), 5th-gen Tensor Cores, 4th-gen RT Cores

specs.label: Peak FP32 (non-tensor)
specs.value: ≈31 TFLOPS; 24 MB L2 cache shared coherently with the CPU

specs.label: Cores
specs.value: 20 Arm v9.2 cores in two clusters — 10× Cortex-X925 and 10× Cortex-A725 (3.9 GHz and 2.8 GHz maximum clocks as reported by lscpu on this machine)

specs.label: Silicon
specs.value: Two TSMC 3 nm dies — an NVIDIA Blackwell GPU die and a MediaTek-built CPU/memory-controller die — joined by NVIDIA NVLink-C2C, which gives the CPU and GPU one coherent memory model with 5× the bandwidth of PCIe Gen 5

specs.label: Capacity
specs.value: 128 GB LPDDR5x, coherent unified system memory (about 120 GB visible to the OS)

specs.label: NVMe
specs.value: 4 TB M.2 SSD with self-encryption (1 TB option)

specs.label: High-speed
specs.value: NVIDIA ConnectX-7 with 2× QSFP ports (200 Gb/s) for linking two nodes; 10 GbE RJ-45; Wi-Fi 7

specs.label: Model scale
specs.value: Up to 200 B-parameter models on one node; two linked nodes reach 405 B

specs.label: Operating system
specs.value: NVIDIA DGX OS (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS base with the NVIDIA AI software stack)

specs.label: Size and power
specs.value: 150 × 150 × 50.5 mm, 1.2 kg, 240 W USB-C power supply; 140 W SoC TDP

machine.note: Manufacturer figures. The 1 PFLOP headline is FP4 precision with structured sparsity; dense BF16 matrix multiplications — the kind measured in Week 01 — run at a different precision and are not directly comparable to it.

method.intro: Every week follows the same discipline so that results can be trusted, compared and reproduced by anyone with the same machine.

steps.title: One command
steps.blurb: Each week folder ships a runner script. Clone the repository on the PGX and run it — no manual setup, no GUI.

steps.title: Pinned environment
steps.blurb: Workloads run inside NVIDIA's official containers, locked by image digest and recorded next to the results.

steps.title: Repetitions, not anecdotes
steps.blurb: Benchmarks repeat the measurement with warm-ups and multiple timed trials; variability is reported, never hidden.

steps.title: Provenance on disk
steps.blurb: GPU, driver, CUDA, OS, packages and the exact source used for the run are captured with every session, plus SHA-256 checksums of the outputs.

steps.title: Honest interpretation
steps.blurb: Synthetic numbers are labelled as such. A stability warning is kept in the record, not deleted.
